rubric.name: correctness
rubric.guidance: Logic errors, unhandled edge cases, and broken invariants outrank all else.

rubric.name: regression-safety
rubric.guidance: This is a large, heavily-tested codebase run in production by its own agents. Weight hermetic tests, behavior preservation, and blast radius: a fix that unmasks or breaks distant tests, leaks live-environment state into tests, or changes shared plumbing without coverage is a finding even when the local change looks correct.

rubric.name: upstream-mergeability
rubric.guidance: This is a fork of gastownhall/gastown that may contribute patches upstream. Flag gratuitous divergence: unrelated reformatting, renames of upstream identifiers, fork-local conventions leaking into shared code, or changes that could be expressed as smaller upstream-friendly diffs.

rubric.name: tests
rubric.guidance: Changed behavior needs tests; regression fixes need a test that fails before the fix. Flag untested behavior changes. A test whose fixture builds the layout the implementation already assumes proves nothing: for behavior that depends on the runtime environment (worktree path, cwd, module root), at least one case must drive the shape production actually takes, or the finding stands (moves the score; does not block alone).

rubric.name: security
rubric.guidance: Untrusted input (bead text, mail, transcripts, tool-call strings, git refs, filenames, env) reaching a shell command, filesystem path, SQL, URL fetch, or subprocess environment without validation or canonicalisation; secrets, tokens or API keys written to logs, beads, commits, notes or transcripts; any weakening or bypass of the town guards (dangerous-command, polecat-path, container-suite, pr-workflow) or of gt done/refinery verification; fail-open error handling in a guard or gate. A confirmed finding here outranks style and mergeability and should block on its own.

rubric.name: fail-open-branch
rubric.guidance: Any check, gate, guard, or measurement whose failure path emits the same value as its success path is a finding, even when the local change is correct.

rubric.name: alarming-branch
rubric.guidance: Any check, guard, probe or alarm needs a test that drives its failing branch and asserts the alarm is observable: coverage of the passing path is not evidence, and a check whose failure is indistinguishable from its success is not a check. Scope is code whose purpose is to detect or report a condition — doctor checks, gates, probes, alarms, escalation paths, liveness tests, and the counters feeding them; a change reporting no verdict is out of scope, so this is not a coverage mandate. Can this check's failing branch produce the same value as its succeeding branch? If so it is not shippable; if you cannot tell, the test that answers it is missing. Rejected example: a doctor check returning OK when its probe cannot run, tested only on the healthy verdict — a broken probe reads exactly like a clean town. A confirmed finding blocks on its own; name the missing assertion.

rubric.name: docs-and-comments
rubric.guidance: A change that alters behaviour updates every doc and comment that describes it. New or edited docs and comments follow every rule in the repository context (docs/writing-for-agents.md); cite the rule id in a finding. A stale or contradicted line in an agent-facing file (AGENTS.md, internal/templates/polecat-CLAUDE.md, a directive, a formula description, a plugin.md, docs/HOOKS.md) is major; elsewhere minor. This criterion moves the score; it does not block alone.

rubric.name: instruction-proliferation
rubric.guidance: An added statement of a fact or instruction already stated in an agent-facing file (the list docs-and-comments names) is a finding even when the copies agree today: the offence is the second copy, and the drift it permits is otherwise charged to whichever later change touches one of them. The finding does not stand when the new copy links to the existing one as its source of truth. R2 in docs/writing-for-agents.md is the rule this enforces; cite it, the existing copy, and whether the new one points at it. In an agent-facing file this is major; the criterion moves the score and does not block alone.
